facts.title: Octopuses have three hearts.
facts.body: Two hearts pump blood to the gills, while the third pumps blood around the rest of the body. When an octopus swims, its main heart stops beating, which is one reason it often prefers to crawl.

facts.title: Honey can last for thousands of years.
facts.body: Its low water content and acidity make it very hard for microbes to grow. Archaeologists have found sealed honey in ancient Egyptian tombs that was still edible.

facts.title: A day on Venus is longer than its year.
facts.body: Venus takes about 243 Earth days to rotate once, but only about 225 Earth days to orbit the Sun.

facts.title: Wombats produce cube-shaped poop.
facts.body: Researchers found that the intestines of wombats stretch unevenly, which shapes the droppings into cubes that stay put when the animal marks its territory.

facts.title: The Eiffel Tower grows in summer.
facts.body: Heat makes the iron expand, so the tower can grow by up to about 15 centimetres on hot days.

facts.title: Babies have more bones than adults.
facts.body: A newborn has roughly 300 bones. Many fuse as we grow, leaving an adult with 206.

facts.title: Sunlight is about 8 minutes old.
facts.body: It takes light around 8 minutes and 20 seconds to travel from the Sun to Earth.

facts.title: Oxford is older than the Aztec Empire.
facts.body: Teaching at Oxford existed by 1096, while the Aztec city of Tenochtitlan was founded in 1325.

facts.title: Sharks are older than trees.
facts.body: Sharks have existed for over 400 million years, while the first trees appeared roughly 350 to 385 million years ago.

facts.title: Lightning is about five times hotter than the Sun's surface.
facts.body: A lightning bolt heats the air around it to roughly 30,000 °C, while the Sun's visible surface is about 5,500 °C. The Sun's core is far hotter, though, at around 15 million °C.

facts.title: Woolly mammoths were still alive when the Great Pyramid was built.
facts.body: The Great Pyramid of Giza went up about 4,500 years ago. The last known woolly mammoths survived on Wrangel Island in the Arctic Ocean until roughly 4,000 years ago.
facts.source: EarthSky, on the Wrangel Island mammoth study

facts.title: Saturn is less dense than water.
facts.body: Its average density is about 0.69 g/cm³ versus 1 g/cm³ for water, so in a bathtub big enough to hold it, Saturn would float.
